edges.reason: Parameter a flows into the addition c = a + b inside safeAdd.
Parameter b flows into the addition c = a + b inside safeAdd.
safeAdd stores its computed sum into the local result variable c.
msg.sender is assigned to the owner state variable in the Owned constructor.
msg.sender is used as the outer key of allowed[...][spender] in approve.
msg.sender indexes balances[msg.sender] in transfer.
msg.sender indexes allowed[from][msg.sender] in transferFrom.
msg.sender is written into allowed and is forwarded to receiveApproval in approveAndCall.
The onlyOwner modifier compares the untrusted caller against the stored owner.
acceptOwnership authorizes the untrusted caller against the pending newOwner address.
Recipient parameter to is used in balances[to] = safeAdd(balances[to], tokens).
Amount parameter tokens drives both safeSub and safeAdd inside transfer.
Source parameter from indexes balances[from] and allowed[from][...] in transferFrom.
Destination parameter to is credited in transferFrom.
Amount parameter tokens is deducted from balance and allowance in transferFrom.
Spender parameter becomes the inner key of allowed[msg.sender][spender].
Amount parameter tokens is written directly into the allowance mapping and event.
Spender parameter becomes the call target of the receiveApproval callback.
Amount parameter tokens is both stored as allowance and forwarded to the callback.
Arbitrary bytes parameter data is forwarded to the external receiveApproval call.
Parameter _newOwner is stored into the newOwner state variable.
Parameter tokenOwner indexes the balances mapping in balanceOf.
Parameter tokenAddress becomes the target contract of the external transfer call.
Parameter tokens is forwarded as the transfer amount to the external ERC20 contract.
_totalSupply is read when computing totalSupply().
balances[address(0)] is subtracted from the supply in totalSupply().
balances[tokenOwner] is read and returned by balanceOf.
transfer reads and writes the balances mapping for sender and recipient.
approve writes the allowed mapping without any prior-state check.
transferFrom reads and decrements allowed[from][msg.sender].
approveAndCall writes the allowed mapping before the external call.
transfer delegates the sender balance decrement to safeSub.
transfer delegates the recipient balance increment to safeAdd.
transfer performs the balance mutation balances[msg.sender] = safeSub(...).
transferFrom uses safeSub for both balance and allowance decrements.
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the destination balance.
transferFrom performs the allowance mutation allowed[from][msg.sender] = safeSub(...).
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner require on msg.sender.
acceptOwnership is guarded by require(msg.sender == newOwner).
approveAndCall executes an external call to the untrusted spender contract.
transferAnyERC20Token executes an external call into an owner-supplied ERC20 address.
The spender contract invoked by receiveApproval can call back into approveAndCall before its effects are settled.
A malicious spender contract can re-enter transfer while approveAndCall is still executing.
A malicious tokenAddress contract can re-enter the owner-only token draining function.

Destination parameter to is only used to credit balances inside transferFrom.
Amount parameter tokens is only used inside transferFrom and is merged into it.
Spender parameter is only used to write the allowance entry in approve.
Amount parameter is only used to write the allowance entry in approve.

Amount parameter directly feeds the unsafe external call performed by the function.
